definitions.meaning: The total of all values divided by how many values there are: the fair-share centre, where a beam of the data would balance.
The middle value of the ordered data; for nine values it is the fifth one. It resists extreme values.
The most frequent value in the data set - the tallest bar on the chart.
A running total of frequencies: each entry adds its class frequency to every class before it.
The cumulative frequency curve: cumulative frequency plotted against the upper class boundaries and joined as a smooth S-curve.
Upper quartile minus lower quartile: the spread of the middle half of the data, read off the ogive at three-quarter and one-quarter of the total frequency.

mechanismSteps: Nine scores, one dot each: nine scores land as dots on the number line; their total is 90, so the mean marker slides in at 90 / 9 = 10.
Three centres: mean 10, median 9, mode 8: the mean marker shares the total equally, the median ring settles on the fifth dot, and the mode bar grows tallest under the score that appears twice.
The mean follows the outlier; the median resists: dragging the top score from 18 to 27 lifts the total to 99 and the mean to 11, while the median ring never moves from 9.
Grouped data: the cumulative frequency table: midpoints stand in for each class, the f x column totals 600 over 24 values, and the cumulative column climbs 2, 8, 16, 22, 24.
The ogive: cumulative frequency curve: plotting the cumulative frequencies against the upper class boundaries 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 draws the S-shaped ogive.
Read-off: median about 25, IQR about 16.7: reading across from 12 (half of 24) gives the median; from 6 and 18 give the quartiles 16.7 and 33.3, so the IQR is about 16.7.
The mean is the balance point, not the tallest bar: the beam balances only with the fulcrum under the mean 10; the tallest bar is the mode 8, a different centre.
objectives: Calculate the mean, median and mode of a data set
Estimate the mean of grouped data from midpoints and a cumulative frequency table
Draw an ogive and read off the median, quartiles and interquartile range
subject: math
title: Secondary E-math: statistics — mean, median, mode and the ogive

trap.explanation: One extreme score drags the mean away from the bulk of the data. The mean follows the outlier, the median resists it: report both when an outlier is present. In class, take the nine scores 5, 7, 8, 8, 9, 10, 11, 14, 18: the mean is 10 but only three scores reach it, while the median 9 sits in the middle of the bulk; then drag the 18 up to 27 and watch the mean chase it to 11 while the median stays at 9.
trap.misconception: The mean always describes the typical score.

workedExample: Estimate the mean of the grouped data with classes 0-10 (f 2), 10-20 (f 6), 20-30 (f 8), 30-40 (f 6), 40-50 (f 2). Midpoints are 5, 15, 25, 35, 45, so f x is 10, 90, 200, 210, 90 and the totals are: sum of f x = 600 and sum of f = 24. Estimated mean = 600 / 24 = 25. Check the trap: this is an estimate, because every value was replaced by its class midpoint - the exact mean needs the raw values.
